entities.title: What init writes into a project
entities.summary: init merges the indexer's stdio server, and zazzle's when zazzled is installed, into .mcp.json, and a PreToolUse hook, their permissions and enabled servers into .claude/settings.json, keeping every other key.
consumers: Claude Code, the coding agent's harness, which reads the project's .mcp.json and .claude/settings.json
entities.definition: .mcp.json: mcpServers.zazzle-csharp-indexer = {type: "stdio", command: <path of the running zazzle-csharp-indexer>, args: ["serve"]}, and, when zazzled is found beside that binary or else on PATH, mcpServers.zazzle = {type: "stdio", command: <path of zazzled>, args: ["mcp"]}. .claude/settings.json: hooks.PreToolUse gets {matcher: "Bash|Grep|Glob|Read", hooks: [{type: "command", command: "<path> hook"}]} after any earlier entry whose command contains zazzle-csharp-indexer and ends in " hook" is removed; permissions.allow contains "mcp__zazzle-csharp-indexer", and "mcp__zazzle" when zazzled was found; enabledMcpjsonServers contains "zazzle-csharp-indexer", and "zazzle" when zazzled was found. Files are written as indented JSON with a final newline, creating .claude/ if needed. Without zazzled, init writes everything else and its first output line says to install zazzle and run init again.
guarantees: Running init twice leaves one zazzle-csharp-indexer server, one zazzle server, one zazzle-csharp-indexer hook entry and no duplicate permission or enabled server.
Unrelated keys and entries in both files are kept.
A zazzle server entry written by an earlier init stays when zazzled is no longer found; init only adds or replaces it.
entities.compatibility: The keys follow Claude Code's project settings format; the commands are the absolute paths of the binary that ran init and of the zazzled it found. The mcp__zazzle permission and the zazzle server name are what zazzled's MCP tool names (zazzle_read, zazzle_find ...) are allowed under.

entities.title: The hook command
entities.summary: zazzle-csharp-indexer hook reads one Claude Code PreToolUse event as JSON on standard input and answers with its exit code: 0 lets the tool call run, 2 blocks it with a message on standard error.
consumers: Claude Code's PreToolUse hook, configured by init
entities.definition: Input fields read: tool_name, tool_input.command (Bash), tool_input.file_path (Read) and session_id. Exit 0 and no output to allow; exit 2 and a message on standard error to block. The message names the zazzle tool to use instead, as an MCP tool and as a zazzle command: zazzle_find for searches (with the indexer's find_symbol and find_references for C# declarations and uses), zazzle_ls for listings, zazzle_read for reads, saying that C# files come as a terse view and that source=true gives the code and the sha edits need. For Bash, Grep and Glob it adds the # allow-raw escape.
guarantees: Grep and Glob calls are always blocked; Bash commands are blocked when a pipeline segment runs a searcher (grep, egrep, fgrep, rg, ag, ack, zgrep, git grep), find without an action that modifies or executes, a file reader (cat, head, tail, less, more, bat, nl) on a file without redirection (tail -f excepted), or sed -n without -i on a file.
A Read call is blocked when its file_path ends in .cs, in any letter case, and allowed otherwise; a blocked Read has no escape but ZAZZLE_INDEXER_HOOK=off.
A command containing # allow-raw is allowed and logged as allowed_raw.
Every blocked or raw-allowed call is written to the usage log as tool hook with reason blocked:<program> or allowed_raw:<program>.
